window.note: PROVED — A NODE HOLDS ONE CLAIM. A verdict no longer lands as one document; it lands as one node per criterion and one per disposition, each bare of ticket and berth framing so that identical claims from different voyages are the SAME node, with attribution riding provenance instead of content. The whole rendering survives as a pure JOIN over the parts, byte-identical to what it produced this morning (pinned by a golden literal over fixture data), so the two renderings are one function and cannot drift. THE STONE SHRANK TWICE UNDER ITS OWN CHART, BOTH TIMES CORRECTLY. The composition half died at survey: nothing in cairn/ reassembles a whole verdict from tree nodes — the only consumers are the exit gate reading the on-disk artifact and the deposit writing — so per its cast kill condition it is parts-only and the count-check refusal was never built. The token pre-flight died at measurement: the host reports prompt_eval_count ONLY in a successful body, so nothing can ask a length without doing the work. The host's own 400 IS the bound, observed live on an 11283-char whole, and it satisfies falsifier (6) more completely than a pre-flight would because no length heuristic survives anywhere — a source-scan tooth forbids one returning. THE CEILING STOPPED BEING FOLKLORE, and the reason it ever was is the finding worth keeping: inference_domain had ALWAYS recorded prompt_eval_count in its cache row, and the embed seam had always thrown it away. The number existed for weeks; it just had no return value. It does now (embed_metered_via_domain, None on a cache HIT because not-reported is not zero), and real verdict prose measures 3.71 chars/token against a 2048-token context — which is exactly why the hand-searched character boundary sat at 7403/7447. TWO THINGS THE TEETH FOUND THAT THE CHART DID NOT PREDICT. A partial landing is safe by the tree's own physics, not by bookkeeping: a mid-verdict refusal writes no deposited record, the berth stands pending, and the retry re-deposits the whole verdict where the landed parts dedupe on content hash. And cross-berth dedup fired unbidden — the drain tooth went RED because its artifact changed only its criteria, so its dispositions were literally the same nodes as an earlier tooth's. That red is the win and now has its own tooth. A1 CONFIRMED, MODESTLY AND HONESTLY: against Stone C's monolith as control, a claim-targeted query scores +0.0130 and +0.0907 higher on the matching part. One margin is slim, and a1 would have been killed without complaint had it gone the other way (validate said so before the measurement ran). What carries it is that the top-ranked part is the MATCHING claim in both cases — retrieval resolving to one claim is a capability the monolith does not have at any cosine. The standing berth cleared: the verdict that refused four times during this chart chain landed as 8 nodes; the next door read drained [] and the DEPOSIT FAILED line is gone. And the ledger now carries both record shapes side by side — a 15:48 single node_id and a 21:33 eight-id node_ids — both read correctly forever, because records of truth are read as written and never migrated in place.
